name: Higher Ground
hint: Two takes. The plate is not on the floor this time — it sits on the ledge at y=14.8, which is 5.2 units above the floor (top y=20) and therefore out of reach of any single jump (apex 3.67). The floating step at x=6.5..9.5, top y=17.6, is the only way up: floor to step is a 2.4-unit rise, step to ledge is 2.8 up and 1.5 across (ledge left edge x=11), both inside the 3.4 up / 6.0 across budget. TAKE 1: run right from spawn at x=3, jump at about x=5.5 and land on the step at about t=0.5s, jump again to the right and land on the ledge at about t=1.2s, then walk right onto plate p1 (x=12..14.2) and stand still. The plate presses at about t=1.4s and door d1 at x=28 finishes opening at about t=1.75s, but you are 13.8 units of running plus a climb-down away from it and the door shuts 0.35s after the plate is released, so you can never cash it in yourself. Nothing to the right of the ledge is landable either — the bulkhead face at x=26.5 is 10.5 units away and its underside is at y=14.5 — so there is no high route to the door. End the take standing on the plate. TAKE 2: your Echo re-climbs the step and the ledge and settles onto p1 at about t=1.4s, holding it for the rest of the take (an Echo keeps pressing a plate after its recording runs out). Ignore the climb entirely: run flat along the floor from x=3 to the doorway at x=28 — 25 units, 2.72s at 9.2 u/s — arriving about a second after the door is fully open. Walk through and into the exit at x=35, about t=3.5s. The door is 5.5 units tall and the bulkhead above it runs from y=14.5 to the top of the world, so there is no way over it.

dialogue.text: The plate is up there. Of course it is.

dialogue.speaker: ECHO-0
dialogue.text: Then that is where you leave someone. It can hold a position anywhere you could stand.
Climb it once for the recording. After that you never climb it again.
